title: What are the sides and angles of two joined equilateral triangles?
description: Two equilateral triangles with sides of four centimetres are joined along a side. The four outer sides are sides of the triangles, and the corners are one or two triangle angles. The four angles are added to check.
teaching_notes: One idea: every outer side and every corner of the joined shape comes from the triangles. Watch for students who forget that the corners on the joined side are made of two triangle angles.

source: Figure it Out (kites and trapeziums, question 1)
video_script.why: The child names the shape made by joining two triangles and reads its sides and angles from the triangles.
video_script.substitution: the book's question with two equilateral triangles of side 4 cm
video_script.anchor: two equilateral triangles of side 4 cm joined along a side
video_script.payoff_line: The shape is a rhombus with four sides of four centimetres

final_answer.value: All sides are 4 cm; the angles are 60°, 120°, 60° and 120°, a rhombus
final_answer.spoken: all sides are four centimetres, and the angles are sixty, one hundred twenty, sixty and one hundred twenty degrees

hold_back: All sides are 4 cm; the angles are 60°, 120°, 60° and 120°, a rhombus
never_show: a right angle mark on the shape
maths_rules: each outer side is a side of an equilateral triangle, so all four sides are 4 cm
each angle of an equilateral triangle is 180 / 3 = 60
the two corners not on the joined side are single triangle angles: 60 each
the two corners on the joined side are two triangle angles: 60 + 60 = 120 each
video_script.design: One idea: read the sides and angles from the two triangles. One picture of the joined triangles stays on the board and the corners are marked one at a time.

narration: <bookmark mark='chk'/>Step five, check the four angles.
<bookmark mark='tot'/>Sixty plus one hundred twenty plus sixty plus one hundred twenty is three hundred sixty.
The angles of a four-sided shape add up to three hundred sixty degrees.
